newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN MONEY RATES END SHARPLY UP ON TIGHT FUND.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN MONEY RATES END SHARPLY UP ON TIGHT FUND.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended sharply higher on Friday amid extremely tight liquidity during the peak of routine monthly payroll demand period, despite the central bank's fund injections, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate closed at 9.265 percent against Thursday's 8.862 finish -- up three percentage points from 6.2 percent finish on August 2, and well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper soared to 9.00 percent from 8.50.
Dealers said banking institutions were unwilling to release funds under the pressure of negative accumulated reserve excess in the banking system.
The central bank's fund injections could not ease the rates because the amounts were insufficient, dealers said.
The bank on Friday injected T$15 billion worth of funds through repurchase of negotiable certificates of deposit offered by interested financial institutions.
The benchmark 86/4 bond yield was stable at 6.1350 percent.
